svg.title: Upload with deduplication
svg.desc: Sequence diagram, animated twice: once for a file whose bytes are already stored (init-upload answers deduplicated and nothing is uploaded) and once for new content (presigned PUT straight to S3). Both end with POST /files/confirm, which creates the storage object or increments its ref_count, inserts the file row and adds to used_storage.
svg.text: The client hashes first, so a duplicate costs one round trip and zero bytes.

g.text: duplicate: no upload at all, zero bytes move
playing: second upload of the same bytes
playing: first upload of new content
folder owned by caller? quota OK?
presign PUT objects/{sha256} (15 min, local signing)
PUT bytes (direct, the API never sees them)

svg.text: Both runs end in the same confirm. A duplicate only bumps ref_count; new content is PUT straight to object storage first.
